record.original_question: Topacogullari proved that for 1 <= h << x^(2/3), D_{3,2}(x, h) = x P3(log x) + O(x^(8/9 + epsilon)), where P3 is a degree-3 polynomial whose coefficients depend on h, and analogous results are known for D_{2,3}(x, h). Improve both the admissible range of h and the size of the error term, derive exact simple formulas for the coefficients of P3, and determine numerically whether |D_{3,2}(x, h) - x P3(log x)| has size about sqrt(x).

evidence.quote: Topacogullari [68] proved that for 1 <= h << x^(2/3) D3,2 (x, h) = xP3 (log x) + O(x^(8/9 + epsilon)) for a certain degree 3 polynomial where the coefficients of P3 depend on h.

Improve the range of h and the size of the error term. Compute exact simple formulae for the coefficients of P3. Numerically check the size of |D3,2 (x, h)−xP3 (log x)|. Is the error term of size sqrt(x)?

artifact.category_tag: shifted convolution sums of divisor functions
artifact.self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $n$, let $d_2(n)$ denote the number of divisors of $n$, and let $d_3(n) = \#\{(a,b,c) \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}^3 : abc = n\}$ denote the ternary divisor function. For positive integers $x$ and $h$, define the shifted convolution sum
$$D_{3,2}(x,h) = \sum_{n \le x} d_3(n)\, d_2(n+h).$$
It is known that, in the range $1 \le h \ll x^{2/3}$, there exists a polynomial $P_3(t)$ of degree $3$ in $t$, with coefficients depending on $h$, such that
$$D_{3,2}(x,h) = x\, P_3(\log x) + O\!\left(x^{8/9 + \varepsilon}ight) \qquad 	ext{for every } \varepsilon > 0.$$
Address the following:

(a) Establish an asymptotic formula of the form $D_{3,2}(x,h) = x P_3(\log x) + E(x,h)$ valid for a strictly larger range of $h$ than $1 \le h \ll x^{2/3}$, with an error term $E(x,h)$ strictly smaller than $O(x^{8/9 + \varepsilon})$.

(b) Derive explicit closed-form expressions for the four coefficients of the degree-$3$ polynomial $P_3$ as functions of $h$.

(c) Determine, by numerical computation, whether the true size of the error $|D_{3,2}(x,h) - x P_3(\log x)|$ is of order $\sqrt{x}$, and provide either supporting evidence or a counter-indication for the conjecture that this error term has square-root size.

The analogous tasks should also be carried out for $D_{2,3}(x,h) = \sum_{n \le x} d_2(n)\, d_3(n+h)$.

status_evidence.title: The Shifted Convolution of Divisor Functions (Topacogullari)
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic formula for the shifted convolution of d_3(n) and d(n), uniform in the shift, with a power-saving error term.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the baseline result with error O(x^{8/9+epsilon}) referenced in the problem.

status_evidence.title: Smoothed Shifted Convolutions of Generalised Divisor Functions (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on smoothed shifted convolutions of generalised divisor functions, refining ranges and error terms.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to push ranges and error terms but has not reached square-root size.

status_evidence.title: On shifted convolution sums of GL(3)-Fourier coefficients (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Improvements for D_{3,2}-type sums on average over shifts, with sigma = 8/33 (compared to 1/3).
status_evidence.claim: Average-over-shifts improvements exist; pointwise sqrt(x)-size error remains conjectural/open.

artifact.status_search_result: Topacogullari's $O(x^{8/9+\varepsilon})$ bound for $D_{3,2}(x,h)$ remains the baseline pointwise result. Recent works (e.g. on average over shifts and on smoothed shifted convolutions in 2024–2025) improve ranges/errors in averaged or smoothed forms but do not establish a $\sqrt{x}$-size pointwise error. No published proof attaining square-root cancellation pointwise was found, so the problem appears still open.
